short: He held a fracturing empire together for fifteen years against usurpers, plague, and a captured father.
full:
Gallienus became co-emperor with his father Valerian in September 253 CE and sole ruler when Valerian was captured by the Sasanian king Shapur I in 260 CE, an unprecedented humiliation that triggered a wave of breakaway regimes in Gaul and the east. Rather than trying to reconquer everything at once, Gallienus concentrated on holding the Danube and Italy, reformed the army by creating a mobile cavalry reserve independent of the frontier legions, and largely excluded senators from military command.

His reign faced an almost continuous succession of rival emperors raised by discontented armies, historically counted among the so-called Thirty Tyrants, alongside the Gothic invasions and the ongoing Plague of Cyprian. Gallienus was assassinated by his own officers while besieging a usurper at Milan in September 268 CE, but the mobile army and administrative reforms he built gave his successors the tools to begin restoring the empire.
